descriptionChirho: The proper name Sheba (Hebrew sheva), referring to several persons and a region in the Hebrew Bible: (1) a grandson of Cush (Gen 10:7), (2) a son of Joktan (Gen 10:28), (3) a grandson of Abraham through Keturah (Gen 25:3), and (4) the wealthy Arabian kingdom whose queen visited Solomon (1 Kgs 10). All three sense clusters represent grammatical variants of the same proper noun across different syntactic contexts (standalone, with prepositions, with conjunctions). Multilingual evidence uniformly treats these as one name: Spanish 'Seba/Saba/Sheva,' Arabic 'shaba/saba,' Hindi 'shaba/sheba,' Korean 'seuba/siba,' Swahili 'Sheba/Wasabayo.' The slight spelling variations (Sheba vs. Sheva vs. Sebam) reflect transliteration differences, not distinct referents in the Hebrew text.
